summary: Final update, validated (valid; single effect: the statement of the status/command invariant entry 46cee4f4). It removes the last wording conflict inside the knowledge base: that entry implied startPhase1 always replaces a missing recovery command with state.NOOP(), whereas the source substitutes NOOP only when the batch it is handed is nil, and the recorded empty-slice path hands it a non-nil empty slice - which is precisely why an instance can end up PREACCEPTED with a command list of length zero. The entry now states that condition and points at the exception, while its command-carrying writers, acceptor-status claim, conditions, sources and executions are untouched and the empty-slice entry keeps its own account. Audit state at the close of the run: six questions, all explained - four asserted recovery-value defects (fabricated self ballot and skipped lower-ballot replies for a non-owner recoverer, equal-ballot replies that replace the command at the slow-quorum trigger position with no later reply able to re-open the decision, the status-guard stall cleared only by the executor's retry, and the empty-slice replacement that also bypasses the client re-offer), one holding contract (client completion through re-propose for the single-NOOP case), and one refuted reachability claim (the wrong-row write in handlePreAccept is latent in this snapshot). Statements, conditions, dependency pointers and citation sets are mutually consistent across the two facts and the behaviour entries after this and the preceding corrections; every measurement cited comes from a controller receipt with its fixed experiment, harness revision and comparison outcomes recorded, and the captured source tree was never modified. Work available but unspent: a configuration with differing value ballots or a second post-trigger quorum re-reach, both shown unreachable in this path, and source-level checks of the executor's handling of the zero-length batch, which no run exercised.
